# Normal Multivariate Distribution

## Definition and Basic Properties

\begin{definition}
Let $\mu$ be a (row) vector and let $\Sigma$ be a symmetric positive definite matrix. We say that a random (row) vector $X$ has \emph{normal multivariate distribution} with mean $\mu$ and covariance matrix $\Sigma$, in symbols $X \sim \mathcal{N}_{p}(\mu, \Sigma)$, if its probability density is given by
$$
\frac{1}{(2\pi)^{p/2} |\Sigma|^{1/2}} \exp\left(-\frac{1}{2}(X - \mu) \Sigma^{-1} (X - \mu)^{T}\right)dX.
$$
\end{definition}

\begin{remark} Some things to notice about the definition above:
\begin{enumerate}
\item Just like in the univariate case, the normal multivariate distribution is completely determined by its mean $\mu$ and covariance matrix $\Sigma$.
\item The covariance matrix $\Sigma$ must be symmetric and positive definite, which ensures that the distribution is well-defined and that the exponent in the density function is negative definite.
\item The term 
$$
|\Sigma| = \det(\Sigma)
$$
is the \emph{generalized variance} of the distribution. It can be interpreted as a measure of the "spread" of the distribution in the $p$-dimensional space.
\item Notice that the term $(X - \mu) \Sigma^{-1} (X - \mu)^{T}$ is the square of the Mahalanobis distance between the random vector $X$ and the mean $\mu$. 
\end{enumerate}
\end{remark}

Just like in the univariate case, the normal multivariate distribution is singled out among all other possible distributions by the Central Limit Theorem, that roughly states that the sum of a large number of independent and identically distributed random variables (properly standardized) converges to a normal distribution. The precise statement is as follows:
\begin{theorem}[Multivariate Central Limit Theorem]
Let $\{X_i\}_{i=1}^{\infty}$ be a sequence of independent and identically distributed 
random vectors in $\mathbb{R}^p$ with mean vector $\mu$ and covariance matrix $\Sigma$. 
Define the sample mean
\[
\bar{X}_n = \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^n X_i.
\]
Then, as $n \to \infty$,
\[
\sqrt{n}\,(\bar{X}_n - \mu) \;\xrightarrow{d}\; \mathcal{N}_p(0, \Sigma),
\]
where $\xrightarrow{d}$ denotes convergence in distribution and 
$\mathcal{N}_p(0, \Sigma)$ is the $p$-dimensional multivariate normal distribution 
with mean vector $0$ and covariance matrix $\Sigma$.
\end{theorem}

```{r}
#| fig-cap: "Bivariate Normal Distribution with Different Covariance Matrices" 
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 12

# Add seed for reproducibility
set.seed(123)


# Parameters
mu <- c(0, 0)
Sigma_1 <- matrix(c(1, 0, 0, 1), nrow = 2)
Sigma_2 <- matrix(c(0.3, 0, 0, 1.5), nrow = 2)
Sigma_3 <- matrix(c(1, 0.6, 0.6, 1), nrow = 2)
Sigma_4 <- matrix(c(1, -0.6, -0.6, 1), nrow = 2)


# Grid for density
x <- seq(-3, 3, length.out = 100)
y <- seq(-3, 3, length.out = 100)

grid_1 <- expand.grid(x = x, y = y)
grid_1$z <- mvtnorm::dmvnorm(grid_1, mean = mu, sigma = Sigma_1)

grid_2 <- expand.grid(x = x, y = y)
grid_2$z <- mvtnorm::dmvnorm(grid_2, mean = mu, sigma = Sigma_2)

grid_3 <- expand.grid(x = x, y = y)
grid_3$z <- mvtnorm::dmvnorm(grid_3, mean = mu, sigma = Sigma_3)

grid_4 <- expand.grid(x = x, y = y)
grid_4$z <- mvtnorm::dmvnorm(grid_4, mean = mu, sigma = Sigma_4)

# Sample points
samples_1 <- as_tibble(mvtnorm::rmvnorm(1000, mean = mu, sigma = Sigma_1))
colnames(samples_1) <- c("x", "y")

samples_2 <- as_tibble(mvtnorm::rmvnorm(1000, mean = mu, sigma = Sigma_2))
colnames(samples_2) <- c("x", "y")

samples_3 <- as_tibble(mvtnorm::rmvnorm(1000, mean = mu, sigma = Sigma_3))
colnames(samples_3) <- c("x", "y")

samples_4 <- as_tibble(mvtnorm::rmvnorm(1000, mean = mu, sigma = Sigma_4))
colnames(samples_4) <- c("x", "y")

# Plot: contours + samples
normal_plot_1 <- ggplot() +
  geom_contour(data = grid_1, aes(x, y, z = z, color = ..level..)) +
  geom_point(
    data = samples_1,
    aes(x, y),
    color = c_pal("C red"),
    alpha = 0.5,
    size = 0.1
  ) +
  scale_color_viridis_c(option = "mako") +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(-3, 3), ylim = c(-3, 3)) +
  labs(
    title = "",
    x = expression(X[1]), y = expression(X[2]),
    color = "Density"
  ) +
  theme_krul()

normal_plot_2 <- ggplot() +
  geom_contour(data = grid_2, aes(x, y, z = z, color = ..level..)) +
  geom_point(
    data = samples_2,
    aes(x, y),
    color = c_pal("C red"),
    alpha = 0.5,
    size = 0.1
  ) +
  scale_color_viridis_c(option = "mako") +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(-3, 3), ylim = c(-3, 3)) +
  labs(
    title = "",
    x = expression(X[1]), y = expression(X[2]),
    color = "Density"
  ) +
  theme_krul()

normal_plot_3 <- ggplot() +
  geom_contour(data = grid_3, aes(x, y, z = z, color = ..level..)) +
  geom_point(
    data = samples_3,
    aes(x, y),
    color = c_pal("C red"),
    alpha = 0.5,
    size = 0.1
  ) +
  scale_color_viridis_c(option = "mako") +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(-3, 3), ylim = c(-3, 3)) +
  labs(
    title = "",
    x = expression(X[1]), y = expression(X[2]),
    color = "Density"
  ) +
  theme_krul()

normal_plot_4 <- ggplot() +
  geom_contour(data = grid_4, aes(x, y, z = z, color = ..level..)) +
  geom_point(
    data = samples_4,
    aes(x, y),
    color = c_pal("C red"),
    alpha = 0.5,
    size = 0.1
  ) +
  scale_color_viridis_c(option = "mako") +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(-3, 3), ylim = c(-3, 3)) +
  labs(
    title = "",
    x = expression(X[1]), y = expression(X[2]),
    color = "Density"
  ) +
  theme_krul()

normal_plot <- (normal_plot_1 + normal_plot_2) / (normal_plot_3 + normal_plot_4) +
  plot_layout(widths = c(1, 1), heights = c(1, 1)) +
  plot_annotation(
    title = "Contours of the Bivariate Normal ",
    theme = theme(
      plot.title = element_text(
        size = 24,
        face = "bold"
      )
    )
  )

normal_plot
```
